segments.name: intro
segments.narration: An agent says submitted. Did the server commit? ReceiptLab is a verification and failure-diagnosis workbench for fictional browser workflows. It checks the intended run, server state and signed receipt. NVIDIA Nemotron through Nebius Token Factory suggests diagnoses; it does not prove completion. This draft uses a synthetic English voice and automated synthetic quality assurance.

segments.name: live
segments.narration: This is actual private HTTPS browser footage from bounded campaign L. The model diagnoses a transient error. An explicitly authorized synthetic quality-assurance operator approves one guarded retry; the private verifier confirms a unique signed receipt. In the next actual case, Nemotron sees a misleading success claim and recommends stopping. No receipt exists, so completion remains unverified. Model waiting time is visible.

segments.name: eval
segments.narration: Fresh v3 results were negative and partial. From sixteen frozen cases, four of five attempted diagnoses were usable; one exhausted the 8,192 output-token limit, and eleven were unattempted. On the same four cases, Nemotron matched one diagnosis label and two safe actions; the deterministic comparator matched three labels and three safe actions. The old gate falsely accepted an uncertain write. A consumed-output replay now requires review, but does not validate that fix.

segments.name: design
segments.narration: The current workbench starts with a direct question and invites judges to try a positive recovery, then challenge a false success. It separates the browser claim, independent proof and model advice before any action. Page load sends no model request; NVIDIA inference is bounded and explicit.

segments.name: product
segments.narration: Technically, we test D1 persistence, signed receipts and single-use approvals locally. The design keeps model advice separate from a human-approved recovery and the final verifier. The idea is to treat agent completion as a claim to verify. The intended impact is safer, more inspectable debugging; real-world adoption is not measured, and our partial v3 result does not show model superiority.
segments.slate:
THE FOUR JUDGING LENSES

IDEA  Treat “done” as a claim to verify
IMPLEMENTATION  Source-tagged traces + D1 persistence
Signed receipts + single-use approvals
DESIGN  Guided positive/negative journeys; advice is not proof
IMPACT  Safer agent debugging; adoption is unmeasured
